description_summary: 12-month unduplicated enrollment headcounts for undergraduate and graduate students, broken down by enrollment level, sex, and nine race/ethnicity categories. Each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS institution ID (UNITID) and enrollment level (EFFYLEV).

12-month instructional activity totals for undergraduate and graduate students, reported as credit hours and/or contact hours delivered. Records are organized by institution and instructional activity level, with the measures used to derive 12-month full-time-equivalent enrollment.

Awards and degrees conferred from July 1, 2010, through June 30, 2011, by six-digit CIP program, award level, first or second major, race/ethnicity, and gender. The table covers awards reported by participating IPEDS postsecondary institutions for certificate and degree programs; each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, CIPCODE, MAJORNUM, and AWLEVEL. It includes total awards and awards for men and women overall and within each of the nine race/ethnicity categories.
Fall enrollment counts broken down by gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFLEVEL.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by race/ethnicity, gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level, with counts for all nine race/ethnicity categories. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFALEVEL.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by age category, gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, EFBAGE, and LSTUDY. Age enrollments are optional in even-numbered years; because 2011 is odd-numbered, age data are collected in this year.

First-time freshman counts broken down by state of residence, including counts who graduated from high school the previous year. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFCSTATE. Residence enrollments are optional in odd-numbered years, so 2011 (odd) has optional, potentially incomplete data.

Institution-level measures of total entering class, first-year retention rate, and student-to-faculty ratio. The measures apply only to institutions with undergraduate students; only academic-year institutions report entering-class data, and institutions offering short programs of less than one year do not have retention data.

Institution-level finance data for public institutions using GASB 34/35, including revenues by source, expenditures by category, and assets and liabilities. Each record is uniquely identified by the institution.

Institution-level finance data for private not-for-profit institutions and public institutions using FASB, including revenues by source, expenditures by category, and assets and liabilities. Each record is uniquely identified by the institution.

Institution-level finance data for private for-profit institutions using FASB, including revenues by source, expenditures by category, and assets and liabilities. Each record is uniquely identified by the institution.

Graduation outcomes measured through 200% of normal time for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate cohorts: the 2003 bachelor's-degree-seeking cohort at four-year institutions and the 2007 cohort at less-than-4-year institutions. The table includes enrollment and completion counts at 100%, 150%, and 200% of normal time; bachelor's completion is reported for four-year institutions, while any degree or certificate completion is reported for less-than-4-year institutions.

Graduation outcomes for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate cohorts at four-year and two-year institutions, broken down by gender and race/ethnicity. Records are uniquely defined by IPEDS ID (UNITID), cohort and graduation status (GRTYPE); the table includes 150%-of-normal-time outcomes, bachelor's completion milestones for four-year institutions, and transfer-out counts. For two-year institutions, 100%-of-normal-time completion counts are not available by gender and race/ethnicity.

Graduation outcomes for the 2008 cohort of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at less-than-2-year institutions, including enrollment, completion within 100% or 150% of normal time, and transfer-out counts.

Staff counts broken down by full- or part-time status, medical-school status, occupational category, and faculty/tenure status. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EAPRECTP, which encodes the occupational category, tenure status, and full-/part-time status.

All payroll staff counts broken down by occupational category, race/ethnicity, gender, and full- or part-time status. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and SABDTYPE, the occupational and full-/part-time classification.

Employee counts for degree-granting institutions with fewer than 15 full-time employees and all nondegree-granting institutions and related administrative offices, broken down by primary occupation/function, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and SCNLEVEL.

Full-time instruction, research, and public-service staff counts at degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices, broken down by race/ethnicity and gender. ARANK is the row-defining classification combining faculty/tenure status with academic rank; each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and ARANK.

Full-time new-hire counts at degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices, broken down by primary occupation, race/ethnicity, and gender. New hires are classified as permanent full-time hires made between July 1 and October 31 of the survey year; each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and SGTYPE, the primary-occupation classification.

Counts and salary outlays for full-time, nonmedical instructional staff broken down by gender, academic rank, and contract length: 9/10-month, 11/12-month, or equated 9/10-month contracts. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, ARANK, and CONTRACT.
Counts of full-time instructional faculty with contracts shorter than 9 months, broken down by gender and academic rank. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and ARANK.

Full-time instructional staff counts at 4-year institutions, broken down by faculty status, contract length, and academic rank. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, CONTRACT, and ARANK; faculty-status categories include tenured, on-tenure-track, not-on-tenure-track/no tenure system, and without faculty status.

Institutions included in custom comparison groups submitted for the 2012 Data Feedback Report, with the comparison institution’s UNITID, name, and state. The record is defined by the custom comparison-group identifier and comparison-institution UNITID.

Survey-component response and applicability status by institution, including nonresponse with imputation, parent/child or multiple-campus reporting, and revised-submission indicators. The record grain is UNITID × survey component.

Directory information for each institution, including name and location, institutional URLs, active and Title IV participation status, control and level, highest award offered, and Carnegie classifications. UNITID identifies the institution record.

Institutional offerings, award levels, control and affiliations, special learning opportunities, and admissions data including applicants, admissions, and test scores. UNITID identifies the institution; admissions and test-score fields are available only for institutions that do not have open admission.

Student charges for full academic-year programs, including undergraduate and graduate tuition and fees by attendance status, per-credit-hour charges, professional-practice program charges, and published full-time first-time undergraduate attendance costs. UNITID identifies the institution; this table applies to institutions with primarily academic, credit-hour programs using a semester, quarter, trimester, 4-1-4, or other academic calendar.

Student charges for vocational or occupational programs measured in clock hours or primarily in credit hours, reported for the full program length. UNITID identifies the institution record, which contains the number of programs, attendance costs for the largest program, and tuition/fees and books-and-supplies charges for up to five additional programs.
An institution’s mission statement or the URL where it is published. UNITID identifies the institution record.

Undergraduate financial aid recipients and aid amounts broken down by student population, aid type, and aid source. The row grain is institution × population group × aid category/source: full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates are reported for federal, Pell, other federal, state/local, institutional, and federal/nonfederal loan aid, while all undergraduates are reported for total grants, Pell grants, and federal loans; each category includes recipient counts and total and average dollars.

Average net price and its underlying financial-aid amounts for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates, broken down into students receiving grant and scholarship aid versus students receiving Title IV federal aid. The row grain is institution × academic year × net-price group, with data for 2008-09, 2009-10, and 2010-11; at public institutions, both groups are restricted to students paying the in-district or in-state tuition rate.
